summary: Parses the CRT environment string block (dword_8D3EB4) into an array of pointers to individually allocated environment strings, stores the array in dword_8D3E90, frees the original block, and sets the parsed flag dword_8D5A48. Entries whose first byte is an equals sign are skipped. Lazy-initializes a CRT singleton first if the init guard dword_8D5A4C is unset, and aborts via CRTAmsgExit on any allocation failure.

operations.description: If init guard dword_8D5A4C is zero, call the lazy-init singleton routine LazyInitSingletonWithFlagGuard_7218 before parsing.
Walk the environment block dword_8D3EB4 string by string using Strlen, advancing past each string plus its terminator, and count the entries whose first byte is not the equals sign.
Allocate the pointer array via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc sized for the counted entries plus a terminator and store the pointer into dword_8D3E90.
If the array allocation failed, terminate via CRTAmsgExit with the out-of-memory code.

Second pass over the block: for each entry whose first byte is not an equals sign, allocate a per-string buffer with MallocWrapperForNhMalloc, store it into the array, copy the string via sub_58FCA0, and advance the array slot.
If a per-string allocation failed, terminate via CRTAmsgExit with the out-of-memory code.
Call sub_58AA6F with the original block dword_8D3EB4 to free it.
Clear dword_8D3EB4, write a null terminator after the last array slot, and set the parsed flag dword_8D5A48.

unresolved: sub_58FCA0 has no explicit source argument in the pseudocode; its copy source is assumed to be the current block entry.
Whether entries prefixed with an equals sign are hidden environment variables follows CRT convention but is not evidenced by the packet alone.
Caller sub_58A19E's exact role in the parse lifecycle is not established.
